correctness.rationale: Zhao identifies the generic fiber with quotient by G=A[2]⋊{±1} (here direct product because translations are 2-torsion). Each nontrivial translation has no fixed points; (T,−1) fixes the sixteen points solving 2x=T, with a transitive free action of A[2] and residual stabilizer C2. Its derivative on tangent A is −I, age 1. There are 16 such distinct conjugacy elements, hence 16 one-point gerbe sectors with Hodge shift (1,1). Inversion kills odd-degree cohomology of the abelian surface and leaves untwisted (h00,h20,h11,h02,h22)=(1,1,4,1,1). Adding 16 gives h11=20, b0,b2,b4=(1,22,1), orbifold Euler 24. This is the standard global-quotient age formula and is correct under the general smooth over C assumption.

originality.rationale: FAIL: Zhao establishes not only K_V ≅ [A/(A[2]×{±1})] but the factorization A→A/A[2] ≅ A via multiplication-by-two. The free normal translation subgroup can be quotient out as stacks, yielding a canonical equivalence [A/(A[2]×{±1})] ≅ [(A/A[2])/{±1}] ≅ [A/{±1}]. The latter is precisely the classical orbifold Kummer surface with its well-known sixteen A1 order-two sectors and K3 Chen–Ruan Hodge profile. Fantechi–Göttsche global quotient fixed-point/age theorem and standard Kummer orbifold results already dominate the numerical computation by immediate application of Zhao’s equivalence. Merely relabeling this classic orbifold as Zhao’s K-moduli fiber does not supply a new uncovered invariant; no claim of source exact wording is needed for implication coverage.
